Maria (CS): @Tayla quick FYI, AceroHealth sent back the vendor security form with a handful of ambiguous items around data acceptance and retention. Can someone confirm our official stance? :wave:
Tayla (Security): On it. Which items specifically?
Maria (CS): They flagged three: 1) "allowed data types" for embeddings export 2) "data residency for derivative artifacts" 3) "rollover/cascade deletion process" — pasted excerpt below.
Maria (CS): ```questionnaire excerpt:
Q12. Can vendor export embeddings? If yes, what types and retention?
Q17. Are derivative artifacts (embeddings/metrics) stored outside customer region?
Q21. What is your timeline for deletion after contract termination?```
Raj (Eng): Quick answer on exports: we can produce vector exports in protobuf, CSV, or ndjson. We do not auto-export tenant data — exports happen only via API or customer-initiated bulk jobs. Retention: persistent embeddings remain until tenant requests deletion; transient caches default to 30 days.
Tayla (Security): For the DPA wording we should be explicit: "Derived artifacts (embeddings, indices, metrics) are treated as customer data and stored in the tenant's region unless the customer requests cross-region processing." I'll draft exact language.
Oleg (Ops): Also call out backups and snapshots: nightly encrypted snapshots retained 45 days by default. We can adjust retention windows on enterprise contracts.
Maria (CS): The customer also asked whether exported artifacts are encrypted if BYOK is enabled. Raj, can you confirm?
Raj (Eng): Confirmed. If a tenant enables BYOK, persisted artifacts (including any generated exports) are wrapped with the tenant's KEK. When we deliver an export, we can either deliver via signed HTTPS URL (TLS) or provide an encrypted bundle that they decrypt with their private key.
Tayla (Security): Also adding a note: we do not retain customer content in logs beyond operational troubleshooting windows (30 days) unless explicitly requested for audit purposes.
Maria (CS): This is great. Customer requested a concise "data acceptance & deletion playbook" they can attach to their vendor risk review — can we produce a one-pager?
Oleg (Ops): I can add the deletion runbook steps (how we handle tenant deletion, snapshot purge, index tombstones) and the backup retention bullet.
Raj (Eng): I'll provide an API example and export format sample to include.
Raj (Eng): ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{tid}/exports" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"type":"embeddings","format":"protobuf","encrypted":true}'
```
DevOps Bot: Reminder: security doc template saved to #docs-templates at 5105005000 — use the "vendor-data-playbook" template.
Maria (CS): Perfect. Can we aim to share the draft playbook with AceroHealth by tomorrow EOD? This is a potential renewal gating item.
Tayla (Security): Yep — I'll draft DPA language and SOC2 scope paragraph.
Oleg (Ops): I'll add ops runbook items by EOD.
Raj (Eng): I'll drop the export schema & CLI example into the doc.
Maria (CS): Thanks team — I'll consolidate and send to the customer once the doc lands. Filing under renewal-risk watch in account plan. :thumbsup:
